title: Dynamic play: count the activity, not only the pawns
outcomes: Lists the damaged pawns (isolated, doubled, backward) of both sides
Counts the activity that may pay for them: open files and the moves of the main pieces
States whether the activity is enough, and labels the verdict as an engine rating, not a proof
Does not assume that damaged pawns mean a worse position without a count

steps.text: Damaged pawns (isolated, doubled, backward) are a long-term cost, but not an automatic verdict. Active pieces, open files and the initiative can pay for them. So keep two lists: his damage and your activity. A verdict from this count is a *practical* judgement; the engine's rating in this app is evidence under stated limits, not a proof.

steps.caption: Black to move. Black has 2 damaged pawns (g6, g7); White has none. Count Black's activity before judging: the queen on d8 has 8 legal moves; the knight on c6 has 6 legal moves; open files: e.

line.say: The engine's first choice at depth 16. The rating puts Black no worse than 0.2 pawns behind: the count favours the activity, not the pawns.

claims.statement: Black's queen on d8 has 8 legal moves.
Black's knight on c6 has 6 legal moves.
The engine rates the position at most +0.2 pawns for White, so Black is no worse than 0.2 pawns behind.
At depth 16 Qd7 is the engine's best move.

steps.text: Activity pays only while it can be used. A closed centre, a trade of your active pieces or one lost tempo can turn the count. *Rule of thumb:* damaged pawns without activity are a real problem; damaged pawns with open lines may not be. If neither side has damaged pawns, there is nothing to count. Compare the three positions below.

steps.title: Paid for, not paid for, nothing to weigh
steps.prompt: Predict which statement fits each position. In the second, a Black queen has moved from c6 to a8; the third is a different position. Then name the one change that flipped the verdict between the first two.

Paper exercise (the app does not check it): in one of your games find a moment when your pawns were damaged. Write your activity list (open files, active pieces, threats) and decide whether it paid for the pawns.
